chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in sheep pens, and he said: “Pray in them, but do not pray in the resting places of camels, unless you fear for your belongings being lost; then sweep it, sprinkle it with water, and pray.”

And I asked him about salat (prayer) on the roadway, and he said: “There is no problem in praying on the open sides that are between the roadways, but as for on the main roadways themselves, then do not pray on them.”

key_terms.أَعْطَانِ الْإِبِلِ: camel enclosures or watering/resting places of camels
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.رُشَّهُ بِالْمَاءِ: sprinkle it with water as part of preparing the place
key_terms.ظَهْرِ الطَّرِيقِ: the roadway or surface of the road
key_terms.فَاكْنُسْهُ: sweep it; clean the place before praying
key_terms.مَرَابِضِ الْغَنَمِ: sheep pens or resting places of sheep

ai.seo_question: Where is it permissible or impermissible to perform salat (prayer), such as in animal enclosures or on roads?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings about places where salat (prayer) may or may not be performed. It permits prayer in sheep pens, forbids it in camel enclosures except in a case of need after cleaning the place, and distinguishes between praying beside roads and praying directly on the main thoroughfare.
